perf.summary: Eliminate redundant self-stores while no duplicate has been seen yet (the common all-unique case).
perf.currentCost: Identical to the int variant: `ptr[dst++] = ptr[i]` stores every kept element even when dst==i, costing len-1 wasted 8-byte stores on all-unique input and keeping dst on the dependency chain.
perf.proposedChange: Same two-phase restructure: scan the already-unique prefix with `for (i=1; i<len && ptr[i]!=ptr[i-1]; i++) {}` (no stores), set dst=i, then compact the remainder comparing ptr[i] against ptr[dst-1].
perf.rationale: Saves len-1 8-byte stores on the all-unique path; 64-bit stores are twice the write traffic of the int case, so the cache/store-buffer savings are proportionally larger. Shorter dst dependency chain.
perf.risk: Phase 2 must compare against ptr[dst-1] (last kept value), not ptr[i-1], once a gap exists. Leading-prefix comparison against ptr[i-1] is valid only while dst==i. Pure integer equality; no sign/overflow caveats.
